It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー|url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/|access-date=2023-04-02|website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} {{infobox shinto shrine|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Koganeyama-jinja Haiden.jpg}} ==Overview== {{神社|名称=黄金山神社|画像=[[File:Koganeyama-jinja Haiden.jpg|250px]]
拝殿|所在地=[[宮城県]][[石巻市]][[鮎川浜]]金華山5番地|位置={{Coord|38|17|52.9|N|141|33|21.6|E|scale:25000_region:JP-04_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=黄金山神社（金華山）}}|祭神=[[金山毘古神]]
[[金山毘売神]]
天神八百万神
地神八百万神|社格=式内小社論社・旧県社・別表神社|創建=伝天平勝宝2年（750年）|本殿=三間社流造銅板葺|別名=金華山神社|札所等=|例祭=9月25日|神事=初巳大祭（5月）|地図={{Location map|Japan Miyagi|lat_deg=38|lat_min=17|lat_sec=52.9|lon_deg=141|lon_min=33|lon_sec=21.6|label=黄金山神社|position=center|width=200|float=center}}}} [[File:Koganeyama-jinja.jpg|thumb|260x260px| Torii gate of Koganeyama Shrine]] '''Koganeyama Shrine''' is [[Shinto shrine|a shrine]] located on Mount Kinka, an isolated island in [[Pacific Ocean|the Pacific Ocean]] opposite the southeastern tip of {{ill|10=ja|11=牡鹿半島|the Oshika}} Peninsula in [[Ishinomaki]] [[Miyagi Prefecture|City]], {{ill|10=ja|11=金華山_(宮城県)|Miyagi}} Prefecture. Its [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|former status]] was that of [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a prefectural shrine]], but after the war [[Beppyo shrine|it became a special listed shrine]] under [[Association of Shinto Shrines|the Association of Shinto Shrines]] . It is located facing west on the middle of the western slope of Mt. Kinka, but since the entire island of Mt. Kinka is considered a sacred area, the shrine and Mt. Kinka (island) are sometimes used almost synonymously, and it is also commonly known as '''Koganeyama Shrine''' or '''Koganeyama Koganeyama Shrine''' . The temple is bustling with worshippers and tourists praying for worldly benefits such as prosperity in business and better luck, but before modern times it was a {{ill|10=ja|11=真言宗|Shingon sect}} {{ill|10=ja|11=寺院|temple}} called '''Koganeyama Daikin-ji''', which was off- [[Shugendō|limits]] to {{ill|10=ja|11=女人禁制|lt=no women allowed|women}} and dedicated to [[Benzaiten]] (Benten). It is counted as one of the " '''Five Benten''' " shrines in [[Japan]] along with [[Three Mountains of Dewa|Itsukushima]] [[Itsukushima Shrine|Shrine]] in [[Hiroshima Prefecture]] 他の五弁天は[[近江国|江州]]竹生島（[[都久夫須麻神社]]）、[[相模国|相州]]江ノ島（[[江島神社]]）、[[大和国|和州]]天川（[[天河大弁財天社]]）であった（『[[和漢三才図会]]』巻第79）。, and is counted as one of the " '''Three Holy Sites of the Eastern Occupation,''' " alongside Dewa Sanzan in [[Yamagata Prefecture]] and {{ill|10=ja|11=恐山|Osorezan}} in [[Aomori Prefecture]] . == Deity == Before [[Meiji period|the Meiji]] period, Benzaiten was enshrined, and in the early modern period her divine virtues of bestowing good fortune were widely publicized, and she became renowned for her remarkable divine powers in bringing worldly benefits such as good luck and prosperity, especially in bringing about financial and wealthy fortune. Her worship has continued even after she was redesignated as the current enshrined deity in the Meiji period. == honorable history == According to the shrine's legend, it was founded as a shrine in the second year [[Tenpyō-shōhō|of the Tenpyo Shoho era]] ( [[750]] ). In [[Nara period|the Nara period]], when {{ill|10=ja|11=ヤマト王権|the Yamato Imperial Court}} was struggling to raise [[Gold|the gold]] needed to gild [[Tōdai-ji|the Todaiji Temple]] {{ill|10=ja|11=毘盧遮那仏|Vairocana Buddha}} ( {{ill|10=ja|11=東大寺盧舎那仏像|the Great Buddha of Nara}} ) as a national project, in [[Tenpyō|February]] 749, news of the first gold mine in [[Japan]] and the gold itself were brought from [[Mutsu Province]] 『[[続日本紀]]』同年2月丁巳（22日）条。『[[日本紀略]]』は同年正月4日とする。 . The source of the gold was Mount Kinka, and in the following [[Tenpyō-shōhō|year]], [[750]] 天平21年春の産金を賀して同年4月に「天平」から「[[天平感宝]]」へ、更に7月に「天平勝宝」へと[[改元]]されている。, Oshika no Muraji Miyamaro and others applied to {{ill|10=ja|11=国司|the provincial governor}} of the time to build a shrine to worship the gods in charge of gold mining, and enshrined two gods, Kanayamabiko and Kanayamabime, on Mount {{ill|10=ja|11=短歌|Kinka}}. It is said that this shrine later became a temple with Benzaiten as [[:ja:本尊|its principal]] image. In celebration of this first gold mine in Japan, [[Ōtomo no Yakamochi]] composed the following tanka:{{Quote frame|[[天皇]]（すめろぎ）の御代（みよ）栄えむと、東（あづま）なる陸奥山（みちのくやま）に金（くがね）花咲く『[[万葉集]]』巻第18所収、「陸奥国に金を出す[[詔書]]を賀（ほ）く歌一首」(「[[海行かば]]」の原歌でもある)に添えられた「[[反歌]]三首」中の1首（[[国歌大観番号]]4097）。}}It is said that the name of the island (mountain) was derived from the "golden flower" that can be seen in the sky. Regarding Benzaiten, it is said that she was a celestial maiden who washed ashore on the Pacific coast of Mount Kinka and was enshrined at the top and base of the mountain, with the base called Benzaiten-do (Daikoku-ji Temple) and the top called Ryuzo Gongen (now Owatatsumi Shrine) 宮田「金華山信仰とミロク」（『ミロク信仰の研究』第1章第5節）。天女の漂着地はいずれも金華山島東部海岸に位置する御船沢とも、銀波越または金波越とも、大函（箱）崎ともいう。 . There is also a legend that King Keibok of Baekje, who presented the gold he produced to the {{ill|10=ja|11=百済王敬福|Imperial Court}}, washed ashore at Omaehama Beach in [[Onagawa, Miyagi|the town of Onagawa]], near the northern base of the Oshika Peninsula 宮田前掲論文。, or that he lived in the same place [[大槻茂質]]『夢遊金華山之記』、文化9年（1812年）。 . [[Edo period|江戸時代]]まではこの社伝縁起（当時は寺伝）が広く受け容れられ、陸奥国小田郡の[[Engishiki Jinmyocho|式内社]]「黄金山神社」はこの産金に因んで創祀されたと考えられる為にその「黄金山神社」に比定されても来たが、[[Bunka|文化]]10年（[[1813|1813年]]）に[[Ise Province|伊勢国]]の[[Kokugaku|国学者]][[沖安海|沖安海（おきやすうみ）]]が天平産金の故地は現宮城県遠田郡涌谷町（旧くは小田郡に属す）であり同地に鎮座する小金神明社が式内黄金山神社である事を査定して再興した為に（現涌谷町黄金山神社）、当神社の創祀に関する縁起も再考される必要が生じた。その結果、海上に屹立するその山容が牡鹿半島周辺沿岸部の人々から神霊の宿るものと意識されて島自体を神霊視する[[:ja:自然崇拝|自然崇拝]]の対象とされていたと思われ、5峰に分かれて「峯巒六十八区、渓澗モ亦四十八谷」とも称される急峻な地形をなす金華山を、[[Heian period|平安時代]]以降に[[:ja:山伏|修験者]]、それも大金寺に真言宗の開祖である弘法大師（空海）に結びついた伝承が多く見られる事や[[Sanriku Coast|三陸地方]]の沿岸部一帯には弁財天を祀る真言宗寺院が多い事等からとりわけ真言系の修験者の活動によるものであったと思われるが、それら修験者が島を霊場として開くとともに大金寺を開創した事が発展の契機となったと推測される小野寺正人「金華山信仰の展開」（『東北霊山と修験道』所収）。。その場合、修験者は[[Honshū|本州島]]の最東端に位置する孤島という立地から金華山を古代[[China|中国]]や[[Japan|日本]]で希求された東方海上に浮かぶ仙土たる[[Mount Penglai|蓬萊山]]や[[Tokoyo|常世国]]といった[[Utopia|理想郷]]に見立て、大金寺を中心に金華山を開いて弁財天を祀った結果、弁財天の授福を司る神格が天平産金の史実及び「金花咲く」の歌に結び付けられたものとも考えられる。なお、仙台藩の藩撰地誌である『封内風土記』には、そもそもは神代に[[Ōmiwa Shrine|三輪明神]]が黄金を練って4本の{{補助漢字フォント|樁}}（杭）で築（つ）いて金華山島を造り、[[Amaterasu|天照大神]]の「正魂」を「留主姫大神」と称して鎮座させたのが後に弁財天となったとの縁起を「旧説」として載録しているもっとも、同書の著者（田辺希文）はこれを『[[先代旧事本紀大成経]]』の神祇本紀（上）に拠って捏造された「浮屠役徒（僧侶や修験者）の妄言」として斥けている。。また、式内「黄金山神社」説は否定されたが、代わりに陸奥国牡鹿郡の式内「大嶋神社」に比定したり同「[[計仙麻神社]]」に比定する説がある。 According to the shrine's traditions, around the time of [[Eiman|the Eiman]] to [[Nin'an]] era (mid-12th century), Fujiwara no Hidehira built 48 temples (halls and pagodas) including Daikin-ji Temple and donated 1,000 koku of {{ill|10=ja|11=寺社領|temple land}}, making it {{ill|10=ja|11=一山寺院|a mountain temple}} (an independent temple organization consisting of a core temple and multiple shrines and temples) with Daikin-ji Temple at its center 月光善弘「金華山の修験道」（『東北霊山と修験道』所収）。但し神社由緒では秀衡寄進の寺領は3,000石とされる。 . After the fall of the Fujiwara clan, the number of temples and pagodas was reduced to 18 and the temple land to 500 koku by Kasai Kiyoshige, who was appointed as the general magistrate of Oshu and lord of [[石巻城|Ishinomaki Castle]] 神社所蔵大般若経納箱蓋裏墨書（[[黄金山神社 (石巻市)#信仰|#信仰]]参照）。神社由緒は清重安堵の寺領を1,500石とするが、これは蓋裏に記された500石と見るのが妥当と思われる（月光前掲論文）。なお、清重時代の18坊とは、大金寺・大蔵寺・大徳寺・大願寺・大応寺・弁蔵寺・弁教寺・弁明寺・弁寿院・斎蔵坊・斎覚坊・斎性坊・斎沢坊・斎念坊・天竜菴・天聖菴・天経菴・天瑞菴（『封内風土記』）。, but the temple flourished under his protection. The background to this is thought to be that, in response to the Imperial Court’s development and strategy for [[Tōhoku region|the Tohoku region]] (the so-called Emishi subjugation ) from the Nara period onwards, the ascetic monks who participated as military forces or military monks in the Former Nine Years ’ and Later Three Years’ Wars and who continued to stay in the area thereafter and gathered at Koganeyama as a base for religious activities such as mountain [[抖擻|ascetic]] practices and incantations, were viewed as being able to provide both prayer activities for peace in their territories in peacetime and military forces in wartime, and were therefore protected by local powerful clans, particularly the Fujiwara clan, who claimed dominance over [[Kamakura period|the Tohoku region in late ancient times. The relationship with the feudal lords is thought to have been similar from the Kamakura period]] onwards 月光前掲論文。 but the state of the temple throughout the Middle Ages is unclear as the old records were lost in several fires. The temple fell into decline due to the wars of [[Sengoku period|the Sengoku period]], and in [[Tenshō (Momoyama period)|the Tensho era]] (late 16th century) all of the temple buildings were burned down in a fire, and in [[Bunroku|1522]] ( It was restored in [[1593]] by the Shugendo monk Choshun Seizobo, who was from Iwakura in [[Shimotsuke Province]] and was also the head priest of Nikko-san ( Rinno-ji Temple ) 『牡鹿郡誌』牡鹿郡役所、大正12年。なお、『封内風土記』は再興を天正年間の事とするが、天正の後が文禄なので時代的には大差がなく、天正元年（1573年）から文禄2年（1593年）の21年間に再興なったものと見られる（月光前掲論文）。 . During the Edo period, it is said that the island was set aside as a sanctuary and the temple buildings were rebuilt in response to the reverence of the Date clan, feudal lords of the Sendai domain. Under the honmatsu system, it was positioned as a Shugendo temple of the Tozan sect, with Daigo Sanboin as its head temple ( the main temple is [[龍宝寺 (仙台市)|Ryuhoji Temple]] under Sendai Castle). Regarding the reverence shown by the Date clan, there is a record of the fourth feudal lord, Tsunamura, sending his retainers to visit the temple on his behalf for three consecutive months in [[1703]] ( [[Genroku]] 16) to donate gold dust 『[[伊達治家記録|肯山公（綱村）治家記録]]』。, but perhaps due to geographical conditions such as the distance from the castle town, there was no sign of regular, direct support from the feudal lord. In the end, only Daikin-ji temple remained out of the 18 temples that once numbered 『封内風土記』。, and as it was a branch temple of Sanboin, its organization and influence as a single mountain temple had been dissolved. As a result, Daikinji Temple, which was trying to maintain its temples and pagodas, needed to actively reach out to the common people. Specifically, it is thought that the temple traveled around villages to promote the blessings of Benzaiten. As a result, faith in Daikinji Temple (Mount Kinka) flourished, and from the mid-Edo period onwards, religious associations were formed in various places and the number of pilgrims increased. However, in 1813, a fire once again reduced the entire mountain to ashes, and the temple buildings were rebuilt to their original appearance with the assistance of the Date clan 奥海登和子「金華山信仰」（岩崎敏夫編『東北民俗資料集（四）』所収、萬葉堂書店、昭和50年）。, but all of the old records were lost during this process. Following [[Meiji Restoration|the Meiji Restoration]], and in response to the Order to Separate Shinto and [[1869|Buddhism,]] Daikin-ji Temple was abolished in [[Meiji period|1869]] and became Koganeyama Shrine, which enshrines the two deities Kanayamahiko and Kanayamahime. The head priest of Daikin-ji Temple returned to secular life and became a Shinto priest taking the surname Okumi. In June of the same year, the shrine was ranked as a prefectural shrine. When Daikin-ji Temple was abandoned, all of its Buddhist scriptures and statues were taken off the island. 小野寺前掲論文。金華山対岸山鳥の奥海家に祀られている弁財天の木像はかつての本尊であったと伝えるが、これは文化期の火災後に新たに彫られたものと思われる（小野寺同論文）。なお、文化以前の本尊は元禄11年（1698年）の記録（『牡鹿郡万御改書』）によれば高さ3[[尺]]7[[寸]]（110[[センチメートル|センチ]]強）の木像であった。 The shrine building had been renovated since [[1877]], but in February 1907, a fire broke out in a house near the shrine office, burning down the shrine for the third time, including the trees within the grounds, leaving only [[Shintai|the sacred object]] and [[mikoshi]] ( [[1916|portable shrine). As a result, starting with the completion of the worship hall in 1916]] [[Taishō period|,]] the current shrine building was gradually rebuilt. After the war [[1952|,]] it joined the Association of Shinto Shrines and became a special listed shrine in [[Shōwa period|1952]] . == faith == [[File:Kinkazan.jpg|right|thumb|180x180px| Koganeyama as seen from the Oshika Peninsula]] Koganeyama was an object of worship for the people living along the coast of the Oshika Peninsula in ancient times, and is thought to have been worshipped especially by fishermen as the guardian deity of fishing and safety at sea. Although this is an example from later times, fishermen engaged in deep sea fishing such as [[Skipjack tuna|bonito]] fishing would call the area where about one third of Koganeyama sank below the horizon (about 20 nautical miles ) "San no gote (Third Palace)," which was then renamed "Nino gote (Second Palace)," and the point where the island's silhouette was small and looked like a star (about 45 nautical miles) was called "Nioboshi (Nyuho star)," and when it was completely below the horizon it was called "Yamanashi (no mountain)." They used Koganeyama as a guide for measuring the distance to fishing grounds, and even when the mountain was in "Yamanashi" where the shape of the mountain could not be seen, it was customary to face Koganeyama at sunset and offer [[Eternal flame|a lamp]] to pray. It is also said that they felt an indescribable sense of relief when they saw "Nioboshi" on their return from the deep seas. In addition, before setting out to fish, it is said that prayers are offered at Mount Kinka, and that on island beaches where the mountain's shape can be seen, prayers are always offered at New Year's and other times Also, it is said that ships passing offshore would light lamps, scatter [[rice]] into the sea, and offer prayers, and that when fishing for pacific saury, seven pacific saury would be offered into the sea to pray for safe fishing and a good catch. 『宮城県百科事典』（河北新報社、昭和57年）「金華山信仰」。 Sailors on sea routes also worshipped him as a god for safe voyages. On the voyage of the Kaisei Maru, a warship of the [[Ansei|Sendai]] domain in [[1858]], the sailors chanted "Oyama Oyama" for Mount Kinka, and when they came into view of Daikinji Temple, they washed their hands, rinsed their mouths, and scattered rice into the sea before bowing. [[小野寺鳳谷]]『開成丸航海日誌』。 一方、古代から中世にかけて金華山に集まった修験者は大金寺を建立し、そこを拠点に峰々を巡る山中抖擻の修行に励んだと見られる。金華山修験の実態を伝える史料はないが、かつては島の東側に「[[Mandala of the Two Realms|金剛界]]」「胎蔵界」と呼ばれる所があったといい、現存する島内の「胎内潜り」や「蘇字（そじゅ）峠」、「天狗相撲取場」といった地名が修験に関するものと思われる事や、山頂の大海祇神社（旧竜蔵権現）の傍らに護摩壇が組まれている事は、修験者の山中抖擻が行われた事を窺わせる。特に胎内潜りは修行の場である山を母胎と見る修験道の思想を体現するもので、巨岩の基部に空いた腹這いになって潜れる程度の穴を抜ける事で新たな験力を獲得して生まれ変わるという擬死再生の儀礼も行われていたと思われ、また、金華山の北東部海岸に位置する「賽の河原」は、そこを訪れると亡き縁者の声が聞けると言われているので、山形県の山寺（立石寺）や青森県恐山の菩提寺と同様に祖霊・精霊の籠もる霊地としての信仰もあったと思われる。その大金寺における弁財天信仰は早くからのもので、それは『封内風土記』に載録する秀衡建立という48坊の坊名の頭文字が「大弁斎天」（大弁財天）の語呂合わせとなっている事にも窺えるが 但し同書に見える坊の実数は下記19寺4院12坊9菴からなる44坊（下線は清重時代の18坊にも存続した）。 、三陸沿岸部一帯に分布する弁財天の伝承、特に[[陸前地方]]の沿岸部一帯には漂着伝承を伴う河神（水神）としての弁財天信仰が盛んで、上述の如く金華山弁財天も海岸に漂着したとの伝えが共通している事から、元来は水神としての弁財天に対する信仰が基になったと考えられ、そこには主として沿岸部の漁民に抱かれた海の彼方からの漂着物を神聖視する古い[[寄神信仰|寄神（よりがみ）信仰]]も窺えるのであるが、そうした基層信仰に修験者が東方海上の理想郷像を重ね、その理想郷を現実に表出すべく図り、その方途として弁財天の財運を齎す（もたらす）福神的側面を強調し、天平産金の史実及び「金花咲く」の歌とその福徳とを結び付けて盛んに喧伝したものと考えられる。{{Quote box|＜拾遺 その1＞'''蘇字峠''' [[ファイル:Gthumb.svg|左]] 蘇字峠は金華山の東山中に位置し{{ウィキ座標|38|17|28.3|N|141|34|25.4|E|scale:25000|※|name=蘇字峠}}、開山上人（成蔵坊長俊）が[[千日廻峰行]]を行った地で俗人不入の聖地とされていた。その基底には山中の奥深い地に理想郷が存在するという[[山中他界|山中他界観]]があり、一種の[[隠れ里]]的存在とされていたようであるが、或いは江戸時代に金銀島としての金華山像が形成された後にそれを更に局地化、矮小化した「すこぶる近世的所産」によるものとも思われる。|width=30%}}The result of these efforts was the expansion of the area of faith in Mount Kinka in the early modern period, but on the inside of the lid of the Great Hannya Sutra storage box dated [[1583]] and still kept at Kinkazan Shrine, there is an inscribed mandala featuring [[Mandala|Benzaiten]], who was widely known in the Middle Ages, surrounded by other deities of good fortune, proving that the connection between Daikinji Temple and the people through the faith in Benzaiten as a deity of good fortune also dates back to before the early modern period . '''Belief in Mount Kinka''' became popular in the early modern period. The background to this is thought to be that Daikinji Temple and the ascetic monks based there, feeling a sense of crisis after losing the active protection from powerful people such as feudal lords and feudal lords, sought to expand the area of their faith by appealing to the general public in order to maintain the temple's management Alternatively, the people who accepted the faith also had a longing for a savior unique to Japan who would bring about a better world, specifically Miroku, who brings abundant crops and appears in the verses of the Kashima Odori dance distributed along the coasts of the [[Kantō region|Kanto]] and Tokai regions There was a belief that Miroku would appear in the year of [[Snake (zodiac)|the snake]] or on the day of the snake, and a custom of forming groups such as "Mi- machi- ko" (a meeting place for snakes) on the day of the snake or the day before it to await the arrival of Miroku. In contrast, Daikonji Benzaiten was also considered to [[Shinshi|have a]] divine role as a water deity, and so a large-scale ritual was held in the year of the snake, in which [[Snake|a snake]] -year festival was held. Therefore, it is thought that as ascetics, utilizing the associations of "Miroku," "snake," "snake," and "Benzaiten," assimilated Benzaiten faith into village faith and expanded the sphere of faith by transforming the existing Mi-machi-ko into '''Koganeyama-ko''' . In addition, it seems that Daikin-ji Temple sometimes held public exhibitions of statues of Benzaiten to raise funds for its temples, and there are temples where the Benzaiten statues were then made into principal images at the exhibition locations. 小野寺前掲論文。例せば石巻市の[[寿福寺 (石巻市)|寿福寺]]に祀られる弁財天像は[[厨子]]内に安置されているが、元は大金寺からの出開帳の際の尊像で、金華山からの遠路の労を省いて当寺に安置されるようになったもので、持ち運びの便を図って厨子に納められていた為に厨子ごと祀られるようになったという。 === Koganeyama faith === The belief in Mount Kinka since the early modern period has focused on seeking worldly benefits such as financial luck from Benzaiten, but at its root is the expectation of the people that there is a place somewhere in the area filled with gold that will one day appear, as they long for the blessings that come from gold production. It is thought that ascetic monks took advantage of this expectation and linked Mount Kinka to the historical fact of gold production in the Tenpyo period, spreading the idea of Mount Kinka as a place where the ideals of the people had become reality, thus expanding the sphere of belief. Eventually, people around Mount Kinka came to believe that gold was buried in a corner of the island, or that Mount Kinka was an island made of gold, even though the island is almost entirely made of [[granite]] and has no gold veins. [[:ja:西川如見|Nishikawa Nyoken]] wrote, "If you look at the map of the world and see that there is an island of gold and silver in the East Sea of Japan, it would not be this island (Mount Kinka) 西川如見『長崎夜話草』、[[享保]]4年（1719年）。 " He accepted [[Europe|the European notion]] of Japan as an island of gold and silver, as represented by [[Marco Polo]] 's The Travels of Marco Polo, and applied this notion to Mount Kinka in a more localized way. なお、[[天明]]8年（1788年）当時の伝聞として、金華山に「黄金満ち満ち、参詣の山道砂金あり」という風評があるが「甚だしき虚説にして、山中においてはさらに金色の石なし」という報告がある（古川前掲書）。{{Quote box|＜拾遺 その2＞'''金海鼠'''（きんこ） [[ファイル:Gthumb.svg|左]] 金華山の近海に生育する[[海鼠]]は「[[金海鼠|金海鼠（きんこ）]]」と呼ばれ、金華山に生じる金砂を食するが故にかく名付けられたといい橘前掲書巻之五。、[[佐久間洞厳]]が、色は濃い黄色で[[鶏卵]]の如くこれ即ち「金気の所化」であろうと述べる等、産金伝説との関連を示している。洞厳に因るとその形は円く裏に傷があるのが特徴で、[[橘南谿]]に因ると他産の海鼠に比べて小さく、味は格別で乾し堅めたものは日本全国で珍重されたといい、[[古川古松軒]]も背に金色があり、他産の海鼠とは大いに異なるとの聞き書きをしている古川古松軒『[[東遊雑記]]』巻之十。。|width=35%}}'''Pilgrimage to Koganeyama and Koganeyama Ko''' 近世中期以降になると仙台藩内を初め他国からも弁財天による福徳の実現を求める参詣者を集め、仙台から石巻を経て金華山へ至る参詣道は当時の一般旅行案内書である『諸方早見道中記』や『諸国道中記』にも記され、それらによると石巻迄はほぼ[[石巻街道]]が利用され、そこから陸海の行路に分かれていたようである。但し、その後の経路については不分明で、渡波（わたのは）を経由して牡鹿半島西海岸を陸路または海路で南西端の鮎川迄向かう表浜（おもてはま）街道と、女川を経由して牡鹿半島東海岸を陸路で山鳥（やまどり）まで南下する裏浜（うらはま）街道とがあったと推測されている。両路とも直接海路で金華山へ赴くことも可能であったが、信心を験す意味からも陸路をとるものとされ、表浜街道で海路をとる場合でも鮎川で下船し、そこから駒ヶ峯の峠を越えて山鳥へ至る半島横断路が辿られ、山鳥に建つ一ノ鳥居を潜ってから山鳥渡（やまどりわたし）と呼ばれる海峡（山鳥の瀬や金華山瀬戸とも呼ぶ）を渡る習いで、山鳥に渡島者が集まった時点で鐘を撞けば島（金華山）から船が迎えに来たという。但し、金華山周辺は潮流が激しい難所として知られ、古来から難船も多く時化の晩には水死者の[[Ghost|亡霊]]が現れて就航中の船に近寄っては柄杓を貸すように頼んだと言われているが、山鳥渡も距離は短いものの「御殿隠し」と呼ばれる大波が頻繁に立ち、余りに風波が激しい時には金華山からの迎船が来られない為に参詣者は鮎川へ戻って滞留する事もあった。金華山に着岸した参詣者は神聖な島へ俗界の[[汚穢]]を持ち込まないようにと新しい草鞋に履き替えてから上陸、大金寺へ参詣し、その後「お山がけ」と称する島内の登拝地巡拝（後述）に赴く場合は大金寺に一夜[[参籠]]して翌朝にお山がけに出立する例であった。また、金華山島は黄金で出来た島であると信じられ、参詣を終えて離島する際には金等の鉱石は勿論、一木一草から砂一粒に至る迄「島の神惜みたまふゆへ」に島外に持ち出す事は[[Taboo|禁忌]]とされ、参詣者は上陸時の草鞋を[[Pier|桟橋]]に脱ぎ置く慣例であり、違背すれば帰船が動かなくなったり沈没したりするとも言われていて、真偽は不明ながら木内石亭が金華山に参詣して島内の金砂を窃かに懐中して帰路につくと乗船した船が荒波に遭遇して進めなくなり、船夫の詮索で事が露見した為に金砂を返却せざるを得なかったという逸話も残されている[[鈴木棠三]]、橘『東遊記』補注（日本庶民生活史料集成第20巻、三一書房、1972）。その後、石亭は学問の為であると島の神に許可を求める祈念をし、持ち帰る事に成功したという。.。草鞋の慣例に見られる金華山を聖域視する観念は強く、大金寺の僧侶が遷化しても決して島内に埋葬する事は無く、その遺骸は対岸の山鳥まで運ばれていたといい、また女性の渡島は堅く禁ぜられ、彼等は上述山鳥の一の鳥居から山を遙拝したという。 Furthermore, groups called Koganeyama ko were formed in various places for the purpose of worshiping Koganeyama, but some appear to have been transformed from existing ko organizations, and some of them were called Mimachi ko, and involved various religious activities centered around the day of the snake. As membership in the group was restricted to men, due to the idea that women were not allowed to join, the group was mainly made up of heads of households, and on the opening days, which were held several times a year, members would gather at designated lodgings on a rotation basis, where they would hang a hanging scroll of Mt. Kinka on the upper seat, such as the tokonoma alcove in the tatami room, use it as an altar, light a lamp, offer [[Omiki|sacred sake]], pray amongst the group, and then dine on vegetarian cuisine . In remote villages where it is difficult to make the pilgrimage to Mt. Kinka for financial or other reasons, a proxy is chosen to represent the group (usually two people), and the proxy who makes the pilgrimage distributes the sacred talismans that are given to the group members. As pilgrimages to Mt. Kinka were made repeatedly, stone monuments commemorating them would be erected at village entrances, crossroads, or within the grounds of local shrines, and Benzaiten would sometimes be enshrined in [[Hokora|small shrines]] within the grounds of local shrines or as the deity of the household . There are various types of Kinkazan ko in various regions, with some continuing from the time of their formation and others disbanding after a certain period of time, but in modern times there are about 500 ko of various sizes in the Tohoku prefectures, mainly Miyagi, as well as in [[Hokkaidō|Hokkaido]] and [[Chiba Prefecture|Chiba prefectures]] . In [[1921]], Kinkazan Shrine reorganized existing ko to form the "Eitaiko" organization with the aim of reviving the shrine and expanding its sphere of faith. Furthermore, the idea that gold could not have been produced from Mt. Kinka, and the historical fact of gold mining in the Tenpyo period was denied in the mid-Edo period. However, there were still many people who held [[遠島甚句|the illusion of an island made of gold up until the end of the Taisho period, as sung in the Toshima Jinku (a chant from a distant island) that was often sung in the Oshika district during the Meiji and Taisho periods]], such as "On Mt. Kinka, there are big boxes and small boxes of gold, and then there is gold as well," and "When a wind of a good catch blows offshore, golden flowers bloom on the island." Similarly, in Matsusakabushi (also known as Matsushimabushi), there was a song that sang, "Mt. Kinka to the east is a mountain of gold." == Rituals == The annual festival is held on September 25th, but there are also other Shinto rituals and festivals such as the following: ; Hatsumi Festival : This ritual is held for seven days from the first day of May, and is a successor to the faith in Benzaiten, as her messenger is a snake (mi). The main festival is held at the main shrine at the hour of the snake (10:00 [[12-hour clock|a.m.]] ) on the first day (the day of the snake), and on every Sunday during the festival, [[Shinko-shiki|a portable shrine is carried]] to the temporary shrine at Kinkazan Port. During the portable shrine procession, a ritual to purify the sea is performed in which seawater is drawn and used to [[潮垢離|purify the shrine]] . This is also a type of [[浜降神事|Hamadori ritual]], and it is said that in the past, the portable [[Mikoshi|shrine]] was carried by young men and rushed down the mountain, into the sea, and crossed all the way to Kamejima (now Kameishi) . In addition, the Snake Year Enthralling Festival is held once every 12 years in the year of the snake. ; Deer antler cutting festival : This event takes place on the first and second Sunday of October, which is the mating season for deer ( [[Sika deer]] ), and involves cutting off the antlers of male deer around the temple grounds to prevent them from harming worshippers. It is said to have started in [[1963]], and was initially performed by shrine staff, but from around the end of the Showa era or the beginning of [[Heisei period|the Heisei]] era (the end of the 20th century), groups of seko (beaters ) from Ishinomaki would capture the animals and have the priests cut them off. The captured stag is given a sacred offering of sake, after which its antlers are cut off. The antlers are then donated to the shrine and distributed to those who wish to have them. [http://www.tohoku-epco.co.jp/shiro/08_10/05doubutu/doubutu02.html 東北電力「金華山信仰と神鹿」]（平成23年7月5日閲覧）。 == Shrine == The main hall is in the Sanbayashi-Nagare style, while the worship hall is a gabled roof style with five bays across and three beams, and a three-bay veranda with a gabled roof in the center at the front. Both have copper roofs. Other buildings include a prayer hall and a Suishinmon gate, and in the prayer hall, goma wood is burned and prayers are offered by petitioners, just as in the Shugendo period. The current shrine buildings were rebuilt piecemeal over a period of 30 years following a fire in 1897. Incidentally, the shrine buildings before the fire (the ones newly rebuilt in the 1870s) were extremely beautiful in terms of their architecture and sculptures, and were even called the “ [[Shrines and Temples of Nikkō|Nikko]] of the Eastern Frontier” 『角川日本地名大辞典4 宮城県』角川書店、昭和54年。 . The site of Daikin-ji Temple is located to the west of the main hall. The pair of bronze lanterns standing in front of the worship hall are one each donated in 1892 and 1894 by worshippers living in [[Yamagata|Yamagata City, Yamagata]] Prefecture, and both were cast in Domachi, Yamagata City. It is 4.8 [[Metre|meters]] tall and is known as one of the "Three Great Lanterns of Japan," along with those at [[Kotohira-gū|Kotohira Shrine]] ( [[Kagawa Prefecture]] ) and Yamadera Risshakuji Temple (Yamagata Prefecture) [http://www5.ocn.ne.jp/~kinkasan/jouyatou.html 金華山黄金山神社「常夜燈」]（平成23年5月30日閲覧）。 . == Temple grounds == The entire island of Mount Kinka was considered a sacred area, and in the early modern period, Ryuzo Gongen was enshrined at the summit of Mount Kinka as the inner sanctum, with Benzaiten at the center. Other universal deities and Buddhas such as Atago Gongen, [[Shinmei shrines|Shinmeigu Shrine]], and Fudo Hall were enshrined in various places on the island, and Mount Kinka itself was considered a sacred island, with Daikinji Temple as its chief priest and governing it. 前掲『宮城県百科事典』「金華山」。 In addition, the entire island of Mount Kinka, including the temple grounds, was designated a quasi-national park in [[1979]] (part of Minamisanriku Kinkazan Quasi-National Park ), and in [[2015]] it was designated a national park following its incorporation into Sanriku Fukko National Park . === Main shrines within the precincts === ; 大海祇（おおわたつみ）神社 : 金華山山頂に奥ノ院として鎮座する。かつては竜蔵三社大権現社と称され、海上守護の神で十一面観音の垂迹とされた竜蔵権現を祀り、或いは弁財天または蔵王権現を祀るとの別伝もあったが、明治以後は[[Watatsumi|大綿津見神]]、市杵島姫神（神仏習合時代には弁財天の垂迹とされていた）、天之御柱神、国之御柱神の4柱を祀る形に改められている。本殿は桁行1間梁間2間の神明造銅板葺、前面屋根に身舎幅よりやや狭い向拝を付す。例祭3月18日。 : 社殿近くには修験道祭祀の名残を見せる護摩壇が東方海上に面して組まれているが、そこではなお火の上に[[Sunrise|日の出]]が来るように柴燈護摩が焚かれている。 ; The front walk starts from the sub-shrine Nameraishi Shrine behind the main hall, goes around the strangely shaped rocks and stones in the mountains, and reaches Shobudaira, then climbs to the top of Musou Peak to pay homage to Daimigami Shrine. The back path starts from Musomine, similarly paying homage to the giant rocks, passes through Tainai-shi, passes unusual rocks such as Kaisan Shonin Zazen-seki and Yamagata-seki, and then descends to the east coast, going around Senjojiki, Sennin-zawa, Ohakozaki, and Sainokawara along the eastern coast, before crossing Amida Pass and returning to the main hall 『神道大辞典』第2巻（平凡社、昭和14年）「黄金山神社」。 . As of [[2007]], there are approximately 530 wild deer living on the island, and they are protected as messengers of the gods. However, there is a legend that [[Date Masamune]], the first lord of the Sendai domain, hunted deer on Mount Kinka 前掲『東北民俗資料集（四）』。, which would mean that hunting was carried out in ancient times and the animals were not protected. However, in the late Edo period, there is a legend that 1,000 beaters were drowned in the sea as divine punishment for deer hunting , so it is thought that they came to be regarded as messengers of the gods in early modern times and later. is [[:ja:分霊|a branch deity]] of [[Kashima-jingū|Kashima-jingu Shrine]] [[Ibaraki Prefecture|in Ibaraki Prefecture]], and since the shrine has a close relationship with deer, it has been speculated that the deer of Mount Kinka were also viewed as divine messengers. 『牡鹿町誌』下巻、牡鹿町、平成14年。 == Cultural Assets == {{Smaller|（件名後の括弧内は指定の種別と年月日）}} ; Designated by Ishinomaki City * Sword Bizen Osafune It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web|title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー|url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/|access-date=2023-04-02|website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} {{infobox shinto shrine|religious_affiliation=[[Shinto]]|image=Koganeyama-jinja Haiden.jpg}} ==Overview== {{神社|名称=黄金山神社|画像=[[File:Koganeyama-jinja Haiden.jpg|250px]]
拝殿|所在地=[[宮城県]][[石巻市]][[鮎川浜]]金華山5番地|位置={{Coord|38|17|52.9|N|141|33|21.6|E|scale:25000_region:JP-04_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=黄金山神社（金華山）}}|祭神=[[金山毘古神]]

地神八百万神|社格=式内小社論社・旧県社・別表神社|創建=伝天平勝宝2年（750年）|本殿=三間社流造銅板葺|別名=金華山神社|札所等=|例祭=9月25日|神事=初巳大祭（5月）|地図={{Location map|Japan Miyagi|lat_deg=38|lat_min=17|lat_sec=52.9|lon_deg=141|lon_min=33|lon_sec=21.6|label=黄金山神社|position=center|width=200|float=center}}}} [[File:Koganeyama-jinja.jpg|thumb|260x260px| Torii gate of Koganeyama Shrine]] '''Koganeyama Shrine''' is [[Shinto shrine|a shrine]] located on Mount Kinka, an isolated island in [[Pacific Ocean|the Pacific Ocean]] opposite the southeastern tip of {{ill|10=ja|11=牡鹿半島|the Oshika}} Peninsula in [[Ishinomaki]] [[Miyagi Prefecture|City]], {{ill|10=ja|11=金華山_(宮城県)|Miyagi}} Prefecture. Its [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|former status]] was that of [[Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|a prefectural shrine]], but after the war [[Beppyo shrine|it became a special listed shrine]] under [[Association of Shinto Shrines|the Association of Shinto Shrines]] . It is located facing west on the middle of the western slope of Mt. Kinka, but since the entire island of Mt. Kinka is considered a sacred area, the shrine and Mt. Kinka (island) are sometimes used almost synonymously, and it is also commonly known as '''Koganeyama Shrine''' or '''Koganeyama Koganeyama Shrine''' . The temple is bustling with worshippers and tourists praying for worldly benefits such as prosperity in business and better luck, but before modern times it was a {{ill|10=ja|11=真言宗|Shingon sect}} {{ill|10=ja|11=寺院|temple}} called '''Koganeyama Daikin-ji''', which was off- [[Shugendō|limits]] to {{ill|10=ja|11=女人禁制|lt=no women allowed|women}} and dedicated to [[Benzaiten]] (Benten). It is counted as one of the " '''Five Benten''' " shrines in [[Japan]] along with [[Three Mountains of Dewa|Itsukushima]] [[Itsukushima Shrine|Shrine]] in [[Hiroshima Prefecture]] 他の五弁天は[[近江国|江州]]竹生島（[[都久夫須麻神社]]）、[[相模国|相州]]江ノ島（[[江島神社]]）、[[大和国|和州]]天川（[[天河大弁財天社]]）であった（『[[和漢三才図会]]』巻第79）。, and is counted as one of the " '''Three Holy Sites of the Eastern Occupation,''' " alongside Dewa Sanzan in [[Yamagata Prefecture]] and {{ill|10=ja|11=恐山|Osorezan}} in [[Aomori Prefecture]] . == Deity == Before [[Meiji period|the Meiji]] period, Benzaiten was enshrined, and in the early modern period her divine virtues of bestowing good fortune were widely publicized, and she became renowned for her remarkable divine powers in bringing worldly benefits such as good luck and prosperity, especially in bringing about financial and wealthy fortune. Her worship has continued even after she was redesignated as the current enshrined deity in the Meiji period. == honorable history == According to the shrine's legend, it was founded as a shrine in the second year [[Tenpyō-shōhō|of the Tenpyo Shoho era]] ( [[750]] ). In [[Nara period|the Nara period]], when {{ill|10=ja|11=ヤマト王権|the Yamato Imperial Court}} was struggling to raise [[Gold|the gold]] needed to gild [[Tōdai-ji|the Todaiji Temple]] {{ill|10=ja|11=毘盧遮那仏|Vairocana Buddha}} ( {{ill|10=ja|11=東大寺盧舎那仏像|the Great Buddha of Nara}} ) as a national project, in [[Tenpyō|February]] 749, news of the first gold mine in [[Japan]] and the gold itself were brought from [[Mutsu Province]] 『[[続日本紀]]』同年2月丁巳（22日）条。『[[日本紀略]]』は同年正月4日とする。 . The source of the gold was Mount Kinka, and in the following [[Tenpyō-shōhō|year]], [[750]] 天平21年春の産金を賀して同年4月に「天平」から「[[天平感宝]]」へ、更に7月に「天平勝宝」へと[[改元]]されている。, Oshika no Muraji Miyamaro and others applied to {{ill|10=ja|11=国司|the provincial governor}} of the time to build a shrine to worship the gods in charge of gold mining, and enshrined two gods, Kanayamabiko and Kanayamabime, on Mount {{ill|10=ja|11=短歌|Kinka}}. It is said that this shrine later became a temple with Benzaiten as [[:ja:本尊|its principal]] image. In celebration of this first gold mine in Japan, [[Ōtomo no Yakamochi]] composed the following tanka:{{Quote frame|[[天皇]]（すめろぎ）の御代（みよ）栄えむと、東（あづま）なる陸奥山（みちのくやま）に金（くがね）花咲く『[[万葉集]]』巻第18所収、「陸奥国に金を出す[[詔書]]を賀（ほ）く歌一首」(「[[海行かば]]」の原歌でもある)に添えられた「[[反歌]]三首」中の1首（[[国歌大観番号]]4097）。}}It is said that the name of the island (mountain) was derived from the "golden flower" that can be seen in the sky. Regarding Benzaiten, it is said that she was a celestial maiden who washed ashore on the Pacific coast of Mount Kinka and was enshrined at the top and base of the mountain, with the base called Benzaiten-do (Daikoku-ji Temple) and the top called Ryuzo Gongen (now Owatatsumi Shrine) 宮田「金華山信仰とミロク」（『ミロク信仰の研究』第1章第5節）。天女の漂着地はいずれも金華山島東部海岸に位置する御船沢とも、銀波越または金波越とも、大函（箱）崎ともいう。 . There is also a legend that King Keibok of Baekje, who presented the gold he produced to the {{ill|10=ja|11=百済王敬福|Imperial Court}}, washed ashore at Omaehama Beach in [[Onagawa, Miyagi|the town of Onagawa]], near the northern base of the Oshika Peninsula 宮田前掲論文。, or that he lived in the same place [[大槻茂質]]『夢遊金華山之記』、文化9年（1812年）。 . [[Edo period|江戸時代]]まではこの社伝縁起（当時は寺伝）が広く受け容れられ、陸奥国小田郡の[[Engishiki Jinmyocho|式内社]]「黄金山神社」はこの産金に因んで創祀されたと考えられる為にその「黄金山神社」に比定されても来たが、[[Bunka|文化]]10年（[[1813|1813年]]）に[[Ise Province|伊勢国]]の[[Kokugaku|国学者]][[沖安海|沖安海（おきやすうみ）]]が天平産金の故地は現宮城県遠田郡涌谷町（旧くは小田郡に属す）であり同地に鎮座する小金神明社が式内黄金山神社である事を査定して再興した為に（現涌谷町黄金山神社）、当神社の創祀に関する縁起も再考される必要が生じた。その結果、海上に屹立するその山容が牡鹿半島周辺沿岸部の人々から神霊の宿るものと意識されて島自体を神霊視する[[:ja:自然崇拝|自然崇拝]]の対象とされていたと思われ、5峰に分かれて「峯巒六十八区、渓澗モ亦四十八谷」とも称される急峻な地形をなす金華山を、[[Heian period|平安時代]]以降に[[:ja:山伏|修験者]]、それも大金寺に真言宗の開祖である弘法大師（空海）に結びついた伝承が多く見られる事や[[Sanriku Coast|三陸地方]]の沿岸部一帯には弁財天を祀る真言宗寺院が多い事等からとりわけ真言系の修験者の活動によるものであったと思われるが、それら修験者が島を霊場として開くとともに大金寺を開創した事が発展の契機となったと推測される小野寺正人「金華山信仰の展開」（『東北霊山と修験道』所収）。。その場合、修験者は[[Honshū|本州島]]の最東端に位置する孤島という立地から金華山を古代[[China|中国]]や[[Japan|日本]]で希求された東方海上に浮かぶ仙土たる[[Mount Penglai|蓬萊山]]や[[Tokoyo|常世国]]といった[[Utopia|理想郷]]に見立て、大金寺を中心に金華山を開いて弁財天を祀った結果、弁財天の授福を司る神格が天平産金の史実及び「金花咲く」の歌に結び付けられたものとも考えられる。なお、仙台藩の藩撰地誌である『封内風土記』には、そもそもは神代に[[Ōmiwa Shrine|三輪明神]]が黄金を練って4本の{{補助漢字フォント|樁}}（杭）で築（つ）いて金華山島を造り、[[Amaterasu|天照大神]]の「正魂」を「留主姫大神」と称して鎮座させたのが後に弁財天となったとの縁起を「旧説」として載録しているもっとも、同書の著者（田辺希文）はこれを『[[先代旧事本紀大成経]]』の神祇本紀（上）に拠って捏造された「浮屠役徒（僧侶や修験者）の妄言」として斥けている。。また、式内「黄金山神社」説は否定されたが、代わりに陸奥国牡鹿郡の式内「大嶋神社」に比定したり同「[[計仙麻神社]]」に比定する説がある。 According to the shrine's traditions, around the time of [[Eiman|the Eiman]] to [[Nin'an]] era (mid-12th century), Fujiwara no Hidehira built 48 temples (halls and pagodas) including Daikin-ji Temple and donated 1,000 koku of {{ill|10=ja|11=寺社領|temple land}}, making it {{ill|10=ja|11=一山寺院|a mountain temple}} (an independent temple organization consisting of a core temple and multiple shrines and temples) with Daikin-ji Temple at its center 月光善弘「金華山の修験道」（『東北霊山と修験道』所収）。但し神社由緒では秀衡寄進の寺領は3,000石とされる。 . After the fall of the Fujiwara clan, the number of temples and pagodas was reduced to 18 and the temple land to 500 koku by Kasai Kiyoshige, who was appointed as the general magistrate of Oshu and lord of [[石巻城|Ishinomaki Castle]] 神社所蔵大般若経納箱蓋裏墨書（[[黄金山神社 (石巻市)#信仰|#信仰]]参照）。神社由緒は清重安堵の寺領を1,500石とするが、これは蓋裏に記された500石と見るのが妥当と思われる（月光前掲論文）。なお、清重時代の18坊とは、大金寺・大蔵寺・大徳寺・大願寺・大応寺・弁蔵寺・弁教寺・弁明寺・弁寿院・斎蔵坊・斎覚坊・斎性坊・斎沢坊・斎念坊・天竜菴・天聖菴・天経菴・天瑞菴（『封内風土記』）。, but the temple flourished under his protection. The background to this is thought to be that, in response to the Imperial Court’s development and strategy for [[Tōhoku region|the Tohoku region]] (the so-called Emishi subjugation ) from the Nara period onwards, the ascetic monks who participated as military forces or military monks in the Former Nine Years ’ and Later Three Years’ Wars and who continued to stay in the area thereafter and gathered at Koganeyama as a base for religious activities such as mountain [[抖擻|ascetic]] practices and incantations, were viewed as being able to provide both prayer activities for peace in their territories in peacetime and military forces in wartime, and were therefore protected by local powerful clans, particularly the Fujiwara clan, who claimed dominance over [[Kamakura period|the Tohoku region in late ancient times. The relationship with the feudal lords is thought to have been similar from the Kamakura period]] onwards 月光前掲論文。 but the state of the temple throughout the Middle Ages is unclear as the old records were lost in several fires. The temple fell into decline due to the wars of [[Sengoku period|the Sengoku period]], and in [[Tenshō (Momoyama period)|the Tensho era]] (late 16th century) all of the temple buildings were burned down in a fire, and in [[Bunroku|1522]] ( It was restored in [[1593]] by the Shugendo monk Choshun Seizobo, who was from Iwakura in [[Shimotsuke Province]] and was also the head priest of Nikko-san ( Rinno-ji Temple ) 『牡鹿郡誌』牡鹿郡役所、大正12年。なお、『封内風土記』は再興を天正年間の事とするが、天正の後が文禄なので時代的には大差がなく、天正元年（1573年）から文禄2年（1593年）の21年間に再興なったものと見られる（月光前掲論文）。 . During the Edo period, it is said that the island was set aside as a sanctuary and the temple buildings were rebuilt in response to the reverence of the Date clan, feudal lords of the Sendai domain. Under the honmatsu system, it was positioned as a Shugendo temple of the Tozan sect, with Daigo Sanboin as its head temple ( the main temple is [[龍宝寺 (仙台市)|Ryuhoji Temple]] under Sendai Castle). Regarding the reverence shown by the Date clan, there is a record of the fourth feudal lord, Tsunamura, sending his retainers to visit the temple on his behalf for three consecutive months in [[1703]] ( [[Genroku]] 16) to donate gold dust 『[[伊達治家記録|肯山公（綱村）治家記録]]』。, but perhaps due to geographical conditions such as the distance from the castle town, there was no sign of regular, direct support from the feudal lord. In the end, only Daikin-ji temple remained out of the 18 temples that once numbered 『封内風土記』。, and as it was a branch temple of Sanboin, its organization and influence as a single mountain temple had been dissolved. As a result, Daikinji Temple, which was trying to maintain its temples and pagodas, needed to actively reach out to the common people. Specifically, it is thought that the temple traveled around villages to promote the blessings of Benzaiten. As a result, faith in Daikinji Temple (Mount Kinka) flourished, and from the mid-Edo period onwards, religious associations were formed in various places and the number of pilgrims increased. However, in 1813, a fire once again reduced the entire mountain to ashes, and the temple buildings were rebuilt to their original appearance with the assistance of the Date clan 奥海登和子「金華山信仰」（岩崎敏夫編『東北民俗資料集（四）』所収、萬葉堂書店、昭和50年）。, but all of the old records were lost during this process. Following [[Meiji Restoration|the Meiji Restoration]], and in response to the Order to Separate Shinto and [[1869|Buddhism,]] Daikin-ji Temple was abolished in [[Meiji period|1869]] and became Koganeyama Shrine, which enshrines the two deities Kanayamahiko and Kanayamahime. The head priest of Daikin-ji Temple returned to secular life and became a Shinto priest taking the surname Okumi. In June of the same year, the shrine was ranked as a prefectural shrine. When Daikin-ji Temple was abandoned, all of its Buddhist scriptures and statues were taken off the island. 小野寺前掲論文。金華山対岸山鳥の奥海家に祀られている弁財天の木像はかつての本尊であったと伝えるが、これは文化期の火災後に新たに彫られたものと思われる（小野寺同論文）。なお、文化以前の本尊は元禄11年（1698年）の記録（『牡鹿郡万御改書』）によれば高さ3[[尺]]7[[寸]]（110[[センチメートル|センチ]]強）の木像であった。 The shrine building had been renovated since [[1877]], but in February 1907, a fire broke out in a house near the shrine office, burning down the shrine for the third time, including the trees within the grounds, leaving only [[Shintai|the sacred object]] and [[mikoshi]] ( [[1916|portable shrine). As a result, starting with the completion of the worship hall in 1916]] [[Taishō period|,]] the current shrine building was gradually rebuilt. After the war [[1952|,]] it joined the Association of Shinto Shrines and became a special listed shrine in [[Shōwa period|1952]] . == faith == [[File:Kinkazan.jpg|right|thumb|180x180px| Koganeyama as seen from the Oshika Peninsula]] Koganeyama was an object of worship for the people living along the coast of the Oshika Peninsula in ancient times, and is thought to have been worshipped especially by fishermen as the guardian deity of fishing and safety at sea. Although this is an example from later times, fishermen engaged in deep sea fishing such as [[Skipjack tuna|bonito]] fishing would call the area where about one third of Koganeyama sank below the horizon (about 20 nautical miles ) "San no gote (Third Palace)," which was then renamed "Nino gote (Second Palace)," and the point where the island's silhouette was small and looked like a star (about 45 nautical miles) was called "Nioboshi (Nyuho star)," and when it was completely below the horizon it was called "Yamanashi (no mountain)." They used Koganeyama as a guide for measuring the distance to fishing grounds, and even when the mountain was in "Yamanashi" where the shape of the mountain could not be seen, it was customary to face Koganeyama at sunset and offer [[Eternal flame|a lamp]] to pray. It is also said that they felt an indescribable sense of relief when they saw "Nioboshi" on their return from the deep seas. In addition, before setting out to fish, it is said that prayers are offered at Mount Kinka, and that on island beaches where the mountain's shape can be seen, prayers are always offered at New Year's and other times Also, it is said that ships passing offshore would light lamps, scatter [[rice]] into the sea, and offer prayers, and that when fishing for pacific saury, seven pacific saury would be offered into the sea to pray for safe fishing and a good catch. 『宮城県百科事典』（河北新報社、昭和57年）「金華山信仰」。 Sailors on sea routes also worshipped him as a god for safe voyages. On the voyage of the Kaisei Maru, a warship of the [[Ansei|Sendai]] domain in [[1858]], the sailors chanted "Oyama Oyama" for Mount Kinka, and when they came into view of Daikinji Temple, they washed their hands, rinsed their mouths, and scattered rice into the sea before bowing. [[小野寺鳳谷]]『開成丸航海日誌』。 一方、古代から中世にかけて金華山に集まった修験者は大金寺を建立し、そこを拠点に峰々を巡る山中抖擻の修行に励んだと見られる。金華山修験の実態を伝える史料はないが、かつては島の東側に「[[Mandala of the Two Realms|金剛界]]」「胎蔵界」と呼ばれる所があったといい、現存する島内の「胎内潜り」や「蘇字（そじゅ）峠」、「天狗相撲取場」といった地名が修験に関するものと思われる事や、山頂の大海祇神社（旧竜蔵権現）の傍らに護摩壇が組まれている事は、修験者の山中抖擻が行われた事を窺わせる。特に胎内潜りは修行の場である山を母胎と見る修験道の思想を体現するもので、巨岩の基部に空いた腹這いになって潜れる程度の穴を抜ける事で新たな験力を獲得して生まれ変わるという擬死再生の儀礼も行われていたと思われ、また、金華山の北東部海岸に位置する「賽の河原」は、そこを訪れると亡き縁者の声が聞けると言われているので、山形県の山寺（立石寺）や青森県恐山の菩提寺と同様に祖霊・精霊の籠もる霊地としての信仰もあったと思われる。その大金寺における弁財天信仰は早くからのもので、それは『封内風土記』に載録する秀衡建立という48坊の坊名の頭文字が「大弁斎天」（大弁財天）の語呂合わせとなっている事にも窺えるが 但し同書に見える坊の実数は下記19寺4院12坊9菴からなる44坊（下線は清重時代の18坊にも存続した）。 、三陸沿岸部一帯に分布する弁財天の伝承、特に[[陸前地方]]の沿岸部一帯には漂着伝承を伴う河神（水神）としての弁財天信仰が盛んで、上述の如く金華山弁財天も海岸に漂着したとの伝えが共通している事から、元来は水神としての弁財天に対する信仰が基になったと考えられ、そこには主として沿岸部の漁民に抱かれた海の彼方からの漂着物を神聖視する古い[[寄神信仰|寄神（よりがみ）信仰]]も窺えるのであるが、そうした基層信仰に修験者が東方海上の理想郷像を重ね、その理想郷を現実に表出すべく図り、その方途として弁財天の財運を齎す（もたらす）福神的側面を強調し、天平産金の史実及び「金花咲く」の歌とその福徳とを結び付けて盛んに喧伝したものと考えられる。{{Quote box|＜拾遺 その1＞'''蘇字峠''' [[ファイル:Gthumb.svg|左]] 蘇字峠は金華山の東山中に位置し{{ウィキ座標|38|17|28.3|N|141|34|25.4|E|scale:25000|※|name=蘇字峠}}、開山上人（成蔵坊長俊）が[[千日廻峰行]]を行った地で俗人不入の聖地とされていた。その基底には山中の奥深い地に理想郷が存在するという[[山中他界|山中他界観]]があり、一種の[[隠れ里]]的存在とされていたようであるが、或いは江戸時代に金銀島としての金華山像が形成された後にそれを更に局地化、矮小化した「すこぶる近世的所産」によるものとも思われる。|width=30%}}The result of these efforts was the expansion of the area of faith in Mount Kinka in the early modern period, but on the inside of the lid of the Great Hannya Sutra storage box dated [[1583]] and still kept at Kinkazan Shrine, there is an inscribed mandala featuring [[Mandala|Benzaiten]], who was widely known in the Middle Ages, surrounded by other deities of good fortune, proving that the connection between Daikinji Temple and the people through the faith in Benzaiten as a deity of good fortune also dates back to before the early modern period . '''Belief in Mount Kinka''' became popular in the early modern period. The background to this is thought to be that Daikinji Temple and the ascetic monks based there, feeling a sense of crisis after losing the active protection from powerful people such as feudal lords and feudal lords, sought to expand the area of their faith by appealing to the general public in order to maintain the temple's management Alternatively, the people who accepted the faith also had a longing for a savior unique to Japan who would bring about a better world, specifically Miroku, who brings abundant crops and appears in the verses of the Kashima Odori dance distributed along the coasts of the [[Kantō region|Kanto]] and Tokai regions There was a belief that Miroku would appear in the year of [[Snake (zodiac)|the snake]] or on the day of the snake, and a custom of forming groups such as "Mi- machi- ko" (a meeting place for snakes) on the day of the snake or the day before it to await the arrival of Miroku. In contrast, Daikonji Benzaiten was also considered to [[Shinshi|have a]] divine role as a water deity, and so a large-scale ritual was held in the year of the snake, in which [[Snake|a snake]] -year festival was held. Therefore, it is thought that as ascetics, utilizing the associations of "Miroku," "snake," "snake," and "Benzaiten," assimilated Benzaiten faith into village faith and expanded the sphere of faith by transforming the existing Mi-machi-ko into '''Koganeyama-ko''' . In addition, it seems that Daikin-ji Temple sometimes held public exhibitions of statues of Benzaiten to raise funds for its temples, and there are temples where the Benzaiten statues were then made into principal images at the exhibition locations. 小野寺前掲論文。例せば石巻市の[[寿福寺 (石巻市)|寿福寺]]に祀られる弁財天像は[[厨子]]内に安置されているが、元は大金寺からの出開帳の際の尊像で、金華山からの遠路の労を省いて当寺に安置されるようになったもので、持ち運びの便を図って厨子に納められていた為に厨子ごと祀られるようになったという。 === Koganeyama faith === The belief in Mount Kinka since the early modern period has focused on seeking worldly benefits such as financial luck from Benzaiten, but at its root is the expectation of the people that there is a place somewhere in the area filled with gold that will one day appear, as they long for the blessings that come from gold production. It is thought that ascetic monks took advantage of this expectation and linked Mount Kinka to the historical fact of gold production in the Tenpyo period, spreading the idea of Mount Kinka as a place where the ideals of the people had become reality, thus expanding the sphere of belief. Eventually, people around Mount Kinka came to believe that gold was buried in a corner of the island, or that Mount Kinka was an island made of gold, even though the island is almost entirely made of [[granite]] and has no gold veins. [[:ja:西川如見|Nishikawa Nyoken]] wrote, "If you look at the map of the world and see that there is an island of gold and silver in the East Sea of Japan, it would not be this island (Mount Kinka) 西川如見『長崎夜話草』、[[享保]]4年（1719年）。 " He accepted [[Europe|the European notion]] of Japan as an island of gold and silver, as represented by [[Marco Polo]] 's The Travels of Marco Polo, and applied this notion to Mount Kinka in a more localized way. なお、[[天明]]8年（1788年）当時の伝聞として、金華山に「黄金満ち満ち、参詣の山道砂金あり」という風評があるが「甚だしき虚説にして、山中においてはさらに金色の石なし」という報告がある（古川前掲書）。{{Quote box|＜拾遺 その2＞'''金海鼠'''（きんこ） [[ファイル:Gthumb.svg|左]] 金華山の近海に生育する[[海鼠]]は「[[金海鼠|金海鼠（きんこ）]]」と呼ばれ、金華山に生じる金砂を食するが故にかく名付けられたといい橘前掲書巻之五。、[[佐久間洞厳]]が、色は濃い黄色で[[鶏卵]]の如くこれ即ち「金気の所化」であろうと述べる等、産金伝説との関連を示している。洞厳に因るとその形は円く裏に傷があるのが特徴で、[[橘南谿]]に因ると他産の海鼠に比べて小さく、味は格別で乾し堅めたものは日本全国で珍重されたといい、[[古川古松軒]]も背に金色があり、他産の海鼠とは大いに異なるとの聞き書きをしている古川古松軒『[[東遊雑記]]』巻之十。。|width=35%}} ==== '''Pilgrimage to Koganeyama and Koganeyama Ko''' ==== 近世中期以降になると仙台藩内を初め他国からも弁財天による福徳の実現を求める参詣者を集め、仙台から石巻を経て金華山へ至る参詣道は当時の一般旅行案内書である『諸方早見道中記』や『諸国道中記』にも記され、それらによると石巻迄はほぼ[[石巻街道]]が利用され、そこから陸海の行路に分かれていたようである。但し、その後の経路については不分明で、渡波（わたのは）を経由して牡鹿半島西海岸を陸路または海路で南西端の鮎川迄向かう表浜（おもてはま）街道と、女川を経由して牡鹿半島東海岸を陸路で山鳥（やまどり）まで南下する裏浜（うらはま）街道とがあったと推測されている。両路とも直接海路で金華山へ赴くことも可能であったが、信心を験す意味からも陸路をとるものとされ、表浜街道で海路をとる場合でも鮎川で下船し、そこから駒ヶ峯の峠を越えて山鳥へ至る半島横断路が辿られ、山鳥に建つ一ノ鳥居を潜ってから山鳥渡（やまどりわたし）と呼ばれる海峡（山鳥の瀬や金華山瀬戸とも呼ぶ）を渡る習いで、山鳥に渡島者が集まった時点で鐘を撞けば島（金華山）から船が迎えに来たという。但し、金華山周辺は潮流が激しい難所として知られ、古来から難船も多く時化の晩には水死者の[[Ghost|亡霊]]が現れて就航中の船に近寄っては柄杓を貸すように頼んだと言われているが、山鳥渡も距離は短いものの「御殿隠し」と呼ばれる大波が頻繁に立ち、余りに風波が激しい時には金華山からの迎船が来られない為に参詣者は鮎川へ戻って滞留する事もあった。金華山に着岸した参詣者は神聖な島へ俗界の[[汚穢]]を持ち込まないようにと新しい草鞋に履き替えてから上陸、大金寺へ参詣し、その後「お山がけ」と称する島内の登拝地巡拝（後述）に赴く場合は大金寺に一夜[[参籠]]して翌朝にお山がけに出立する例であった。また、金華山島は黄金で出来た島であると信じられ、参詣を終えて離島する際には金等の鉱石は勿論、一木一草から砂一粒に至る迄「島の神惜みたまふゆへ」に島外に持ち出す事は[[Taboo|禁忌]]とされ、参詣者は上陸時の草鞋を[[Pier|桟橋]]に脱ぎ置く慣例であり、違背すれば帰船が動かなくなったり沈没したりするとも言われていて、真偽は不明ながら木内石亭が金華山に参詣して島内の金砂を窃かに懐中して帰路につくと乗船した船が荒波に遭遇して進めなくなり、船夫の詮索で事が露見した為に金砂を返却せざるを得なかったという逸話も残されている[[鈴木棠三]]、橘『東遊記』補注（日本庶民生活史料集成第20巻、三一書房、1972）。その後、石亭は学問の為であると島の神に許可を求める祈念をし、持ち帰る事に成功したという。.。草鞋の慣例に見られる金華山を聖域視する観念は強く、大金寺の僧侶が遷化しても決して島内に埋葬する事は無く、その遺骸は対岸の山鳥まで運ばれていたといい、また女性の渡島は堅く禁ぜられ、彼等は上述山鳥の一の鳥居から山を遙拝したという。 Furthermore, groups called Koganeyama ko were formed in various places for the purpose of worshiping Koganeyama, but some appear to have been transformed from existing ko organizations, and some of them were called Mimachi ko, and involved various religious activities centered around the day of the snake. As membership in the group was restricted to men, due to the idea that women were not allowed to join, the group was mainly made up of heads of households, and on the opening days, which were held several times a year, members would gather at designated lodgings on a rotation basis, where they would hang a hanging scroll of Mt. Kinka on the upper seat, such as the tokonoma alcove in the tatami room, use it as an altar, light a lamp, offer [[Omiki|sacred sake]], pray amongst the group, and then dine on vegetarian cuisine . In remote villages where it is difficult to make the pilgrimage to Mt. Kinka for financial or other reasons, a proxy is chosen to represent the group (usually two people), and the proxy who makes the pilgrimage distributes the sacred talismans that are given to the group members. As pilgrimages to Mt. Kinka were made repeatedly, stone monuments commemorating them would be erected at village entrances, crossroads, or within the grounds of local shrines, and Benzaiten would sometimes be enshrined in [[Hokora|small shrines]] within the grounds of local shrines or as the deity of the household . There are various types of Kinkazan ko in various regions, with some continuing from the time of their formation and others disbanding after a certain period of time, but in modern times there are about 500 ko of various sizes in the Tohoku prefectures, mainly Miyagi, as well as in [[Hokkaidō|Hokkaido]] and [[Chiba Prefecture|Chiba prefectures]] . In [[1921]], Kinkazan Shrine reorganized existing ko to form the "Eitaiko" organization with the aim of reviving the shrine and expanding its sphere of faith. Furthermore, the idea that gold could not have been produced from Mt. Kinka, and the historical fact of gold mining in the Tenpyo period was denied in the mid-Edo period. However, there were still many people who held [[遠島甚句|the illusion of an island made of gold up until the end of the Taisho period, as sung in the Toshima Jinku (a chant from a distant island) that was often sung in the Oshika district during the Meiji and Taisho periods]], such as "On Mt. Kinka, there are big boxes and small boxes of gold, and then there is gold as well," and "When a wind of a good catch blows offshore, golden flowers bloom on the island." Similarly, in Matsusakabushi (also known as Matsushimabushi), there was a song that sang, "Mt. Kinka to the east is a mountain of gold." == Rituals == The annual festival is held on September 25th, but there are also other Shinto rituals and festivals such as the following: ; Hatsumi Festival : This ritual is held for seven days from the first day of May, and is a successor to the faith in Benzaiten, as her messenger is a snake (mi). The main festival is held at the main shrine at the hour of the snake (10:00 [[12-hour clock|a.m.]] ) on the first day (the day of the snake), and on every Sunday during the festival, [[Shinko-shiki|a portable shrine is carried]] to the temporary shrine at Kinkazan Port. During the portable shrine procession, a ritual to purify the sea is performed in which seawater is drawn and used to [[潮垢離|purify the shrine]] . This is also a type of [[浜降神事|Hamadori ritual]], and it is said that in the past, the portable [[Mikoshi|shrine]] was carried by young men and rushed down the mountain, into the sea, and crossed all the way to Kamejima (now Kameishi) . In addition, the Snake Year Enthralling Festival is held once every 12 years in the year of the snake. ; Deer antler cutting festival : This event takes place on the first and second Sunday of October, which is the mating season for deer ( [[Sika deer]] ), and involves cutting off the antlers of male deer around the temple grounds to prevent them from harming worshippers. It is said to have started in [[1963]], and was initially performed by shrine staff, but from around the end of the Showa era or the beginning of [[Heisei period|the Heisei]] era (the end of the 20th century), groups of seko (beaters ) from Ishinomaki would capture the animals and have the priests cut them off. The captured stag is given a sacred offering of sake, after which its antlers are cut off. The antlers are then donated to the shrine and distributed to those who wish to have them. [http://www.tohoku-epco.co.jp/shiro/08_10/05doubutu/doubutu02.html 東北電力「金華山信仰と神鹿」]（平成23年7月5日閲覧）。 == Shrine == The main hall is in the Sanbayashi-Nagare style, while the worship hall is a gabled roof style with five bays across and three beams, and a three-bay veranda with a gabled roof in the center at the front. Both have copper roofs. Other buildings include a prayer hall and a Suishinmon gate, and in the prayer hall, goma wood is burned and prayers are offered by petitioners, just as in the Shugendo period. The current shrine buildings were rebuilt piecemeal over a period of 30 years following a fire in 1897. Incidentally, the shrine buildings before the fire (the ones newly rebuilt in the 1870s) were extremely beautiful in terms of their architecture and sculptures, and were even called the “ [[Shrines and Temples of Nikkō|Nikko]] of the Eastern Frontier” 『角川日本地名大辞典4 宮城県』角川書店、昭和54年。 . The site of Daikin-ji Temple is located to the west of the main hall. The pair of bronze lanterns standing in front of the worship hall are one each donated in 1892 and 1894 by worshippers living in [[Yamagata|Yamagata City, Yamagata]] Prefecture, and both were cast in Domachi, Yamagata City. It is 4.8 [[Metre|meters]] tall and is known as one of the "Three Great Lanterns of Japan," along with those at [[Kotohira-gū|Kotohira Shrine]] ( [[Kagawa Prefecture]] ) and Yamadera Risshakuji Temple (Yamagata Prefecture) [http://www5.ocn.ne.jp/~kinkasan/jouyatou.html 金華山黄金山神社「常夜燈」]（平成23年5月30日閲覧）。 . == Temple grounds == The entire island of Mount Kinka was considered a sacred area, and in the early modern period, Ryuzo Gongen was enshrined at the summit of Mount Kinka as the inner sanctum, with Benzaiten at the center. Other universal deities and Buddhas such as Atago Gongen, [[Shinmei shrines|Shinmeigu Shrine]], and Fudo Hall were enshrined in various places on the island, and Mount Kinka itself was considered a sacred island, with Daikinji Temple as its chief priest and governing it. 前掲『宮城県百科事典』「金華山」。 In addition, the entire island of Mount Kinka, including the temple grounds, was designated a quasi-national park in [[1979]] (part of Minamisanriku Kinkazan Quasi-National Park ), and in [[2015]] it was designated a national park following its incorporation into Sanriku Fukko National Park . === Main shrines within the precincts === ; The front walk starts from the sub-shrine Nameraishi Shrine behind the main hall, goes around the strangely shaped rocks and stones in the mountains, and reaches Shobudaira, then climbs to the top of Musou Peak to pay homage to Daimigami Shrine. The back path starts from Musomine, similarly paying homage to the giant rocks, passes through Tainai-shi, passes unusual rocks such as Kaisan Shonin Zazen-seki and Yamagata-seki, and then descends to the east coast, going around Senjojiki, Sennin-zawa, Ohakozaki, and Sainokawara along the eastern coast, before crossing Amida Pass and returning to the main hall 『神道大辞典』第2巻（平凡社、昭和14年）「黄金山神社」。 . As of [[2007]], there are approximately 530 wild deer living on the island, and they are protected as messengers of the gods. However, there is a legend that [[Date Masamune]], the first lord of the Sendai domain, hunted deer on Mount Kinka 前掲『東北民俗資料集（四）』。, which would mean that hunting was carried out in ancient times and the animals were not protected. However, in the late Edo period, there is a legend that 1,000 beaters were drowned in the sea as divine punishment for deer hunting , so it is thought that they came to be regarded as messengers of the gods in early modern times and later.
